name: blur-vignette

frames.best_why: Frame 1 shows both vignette panels cleanly, with the photo and text edges fully visible.

tagline: Edges melt into a soft blur while the centre of a panel stays sharp.
summary: A square container whose outer edges blur and fade into the background, leaving the middle crisp. The demo pairs a dark text panel with a mountain photo to show the effect on copy and imagery.
appearance: Two rounded squares side by side on a near-black page: one a dark grey panel of small white text, the other a photo of snowy mountains above a sea of cloud at dusk. On both, a band around the border softens and dissolves into the page while the centre stays clear.
behaviour: Static: the blur mask is painted once and neither animates nor responds to the pointer. The blur amount, inset and fade length are fixed by props rather than interaction.
demo_content: A dark text panel headed Blur Vignette beside a photo of snowy mountains above clouds.
search_phrases: soft fade border on a card
soft focus border keeping centre sharp
use_when: You want to soften where a photo or card meets the page without a hard border or heavy shadow.
avoid_when: Backdrop blur costs GPU, and the fade hides edge content such as captions or buttons.
customise: Radius, inset, transition length and blur are props on the wrapper, while classname sets size and background. Children sit beneath a separate article layer that carries the mask.
weight_why: One backdrop-blur layer with a CSS mask and no script beyond React.

a11y.note: Purely visual effect with nothing to operate; it has no motion but also no accessibility hooks.

issues: The wrapper forces a square aspect ratio, so wide photos or text blocks cannot use their natural shape.
The demo's small parameter line is very low contrast against the grey panel.
polish_why: Subtle, even edge blur on both text and photo; the tiny parameter line is hard to read.
title: Blur Vignette
